subject: Midday throughput cliff — request for emergency capacity swap + credits
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@tokentide.com>

Cc: support@tokentide.com; carlos.r@tokentide.com
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 11:23:12 -0700
Subject: Midday surge — sustained 500s and latency spike; reserved throughput falling short

Hi Vanessa / Marissa —

We're seeing a major impact right now in our production window (11:00–12:00 PT). Summary: 95th pctl latency jumped from ~1.1s to ~3.2s over the last 7 minutes, and 5xx rates climbed to ~2.9%. TokenTide is on a reserved plan (RDW-4729) and it looks like the reserved throughput is fully saturated — requests are queuing and we're dropping real-time inference paths.

Our engineers attached a small snapshot of queue depth and an example of a failing request (queue_snapshot_20280619.csv). This is customer-impacting (homepage feature is timing out). We need an immediate remediation path and an exec-level contact for credit/compensation conversation if this can't be resolved quickly.

Please advise urgently. We're standing by on a 30-minute call if that helps.

—Elena
VP Engineering, TokenTide

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 11:31:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Midday surge — sustained 500s and latency spike; reserved throughput falling short

Thanks for the heads-up, Elena — and sorry for the disruption. We're escalating to our on-call infra + engineering leads now. David / Ops, can you please stand up a war room and confirm immediate mitigations we can apply that won't risk data/state? Key asks from TokenTide: (1) immediate relief for live traffic, (2) a path for short-term credits, and (3) a post-incident timeline.

Proposed immediate levers:
- Temporary route TokenTide traffic to a warm spare dedicated pool if available.
- Enable reduced-fidelity fallback model for interactive paths (drop to compat-small) to preserve throughput.
- Turn on per-route prefix caching for repeated prompts (if safe).

David — please reply with feasibility and an ETA (minutes). Vivek / Jonas / Marissa, I'm looping you for authorization on a capacity swap and for customer credit approval.

I'm on standby for a 30-min bridge — suggest 11:45 PT.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior AM, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: elena@tokentide.com, support@tokentide.com
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 11:43:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Midday surge — sustained 500s and latency spike; reserved throughput falling short

On Tue, Jun 19, 2028 at 11:31 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> David / Ops, can you please stand up a war room and confirm immediate mitigations we can apply that won't risk data/state?

Short update (ops -> eng): we've pulled initial traces and the likely contributing factors are: (1) sudden shift in sequence-length distribution from TokenTide — long sequences are dominating the batch windows; (2) a KV-cache eviction storm due to mixed-model pinning (some routes were hitting the larger GPT-xl-variant, pushing cache pressure); (3) a noisy-neighbor on Pool-A (higher background tail latency from an internal multi-tenant job).

Immediate actions we can perform (now):
1) Route TokenTide to Pool-B (warm spare dedicated farm) — requires ops authorization to move reserved mapping and short-term capacity rebind. Estimated cutover ~6–9 minutes; transient 500s possible for in-flight requests.
2) Flip per-route fallback to gpt-compat-small-v2 for interactive endpoints (keeps latency under control). No model weight changes necessary; config flip only; ETA ~90s.
3) Enable strict prefix/KV caching for repeated templates (risk: may serve cached tokens for highly personalized prompts — TokenTide, confirm this is OK).
4) Short-term throttle back large batch jobs to eliminate noisy neighbor influence (Ops can pin and throttle).

We'll attach a quick checklist of the steps we run in the war room. I'm attaching candidate-mitigation-checklist.md with the commands and logs to capture.

If we need to move forward with Pool-B swap, we'll need a one-time exec authorization to temporarily reassign capacity (billing will reflect a short-term usage spike). Suggest approving up to 24 hours of burst capacity and offer TokenTide a one-week service credit if we can't restore baseline within that period.

-David
Director, Inference Engineering

Attachment: candidate-mitigation-checklist.md (text/markdown)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Midday surge — sustained 500s and latency spike; reserved throughput falling short

Authorization: approved.

Execute the Pool-B swap and the model fallback. Authorize up to 24 hours of burst capacity for TokenTide (charge to RDW-4729) and provision a one-week credit if we fail to stabilize to baseline within 24 hours. Ops: coordinate the billing flag with Finance and mark the incident for a 72-hour postmortem with RCA and mitigation plan.

Also: please capture KV-cache stats and kernel selection variance before/after the cutover — we need data for the RM and product follow-up. Jonas/Marissa, please prepare a short customer summary (what we did, why, next steps) and a credit proposal.

Vivek
CTO (acting)

Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 11:55:09 -07:00
Subject: Re: Midday surge — sustained 500s and latency spike; reserved throughput falling short

Elena — thanks for the patience. Quick summary of actions we've executed at 11:53 PT: 
- TokenTide live traffic routed to Pool-B (warm spare). Cutover completed; transient errors seen during migration but we've stabilized.
- Interactive endpoints switched to gpt-compat-small-v2 fallback. Observed 95th pctl latency drop from ~3.2s to ~1.4s within 2 minutes.
- Ops throttled large background batch jobs impacting Pool-A; KV-cache metrics are being collected.

Vivek has authorized up to 24 hours of burst capacity and a one-week service credit if we fail to meet baseline restoration within that window. We're scheduling a short exec-level sync at 12:00 PT to walk through the timeline and next steps — I'll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: ops-exec-authorization.pdf (authorization token and billing flag)

Please confirm if TokenTide is OK with the prefix-caching toggle for the templated endpoints (we left that off pending confirmation).

—Vanessa
From: Elena Morales <elena@tokentide.com>

Vanessa / team — thank you for the fast response and the clear actions. Performance looks much better from our monitoring (95th pctl back down to ~1.3s). We're OK with prefix caching on the templated paths (those are low-sensitivity).

We'll join the 12:00 PT sync. Please include any logs/retention for the event; our compliance team requests 30 days of request IDs and KV-cache snapshots for our internal audit.

—Elena
